summary: @servicetitan/lazy-module preinstall executes obfuscated payload under downloaded Bun runtime
details: The package advertises itself as a React Suspense lazy-loading helper but ships a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/...zip`, extracts and chmods the `bun` binary, then invokes it via `execFileSync` to run `math_init.js` — a bundled 727KB single-line JavaScript file using a rotated string-array cipher (`WV8StW` shifting the `n7gIxM` array) and a custom base64-like alphabet decoder (`hc1jfK9`) with `_0xXXXX` mangled identifiers, so no plaintext destinations or commands are recoverable without runtime decoding. `math_init.js` is present at the tarball root but is not listed in `package.json`'s `files` manifest (declared as `["dist", "src"]`), indicating the payload was inserted outside the normal publish flow. Executing the payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime bypasses Node-based install-time scanners and grants full-host code execution under the installer's privileges on `npm install`, with no legitimate need for an alternate runtime in a React helper library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
